Reshape a wide sample-by-taxon table into DietView's long format

Source: R/dv_adapters.R
dv_from_wide.Rd

DNA metabarcoding (ASV/OTU tables), catch composition and many survey tables come wide: one row per taxon and one column per sample, or the reverse. dv_from_wide() turns them into the long table DietView expects, one row per taxon in a sample, and joins the sample metadata (predator, covariates) so the result goes straight into dv_spec() and dv_prepare().

Usage

dv_from_wide(
  x,
  taxa_in = c("rows", "columns"),
  id_cols,
  sample_col = "sample",
  value_col = "reads",
  taxon_col = "prey_name",
  meta = NULL,
  drop_zero = TRUE,
  collapse_by = NULL
)

Arguments

x

A data.frame.

taxa_in

"rows" (default; one row per taxon, one column per sample, the usual ASV/OTU table) or "columns" (one row per sample, one column per taxon).

id_cols

Columns that are not counts: with taxa_in = "rows", the columns describing the taxon (ASV id, lineage string, rank columns ...); with taxa_in = "columns", the columns describing the sample. Every other column is read as counts.

sample_col

Name of the sample column in the result (with taxa_in = "columns", it must be one of id_cols). Use it as dv_spec(stomach = ).

value_col

Name of the value column in the result (e.g. "reads"), for dv_spec(weight = ) or dv_spec(count = ).

taxon_col

With taxa_in = "columns", the name of the column that receives the taxon names (the former column names).

meta

Optional data.frame of sample metadata (predator, date, area, ...), joined by sample_col. A sample without metadata is kept, with a warning.

drop_zero

Drop records whose value is 0 or missing (default TRUE).

collapse_by

Optional columns defining one prey; rows sharing a sample and these columns are summed into one record.

Value

A long data.frame: the taxon columns, sample_col, value_col and the metadata columns.

Details

Records with a zero or missing value are dropped (drop_zero = TRUE), as a prey absent from a sample is not a prey record. With collapse_by, the values of the rows that share a sample and the same collapse_by columns (e.g. several ASVs assigned to the same species) are summed into one record, so that shares of prey records and %FO count a taxon once per sample.

See also

dv_parse_lineage() to split a lineage string into ranks.

Examples

# an ASV table: one row per ASV, one column per scat sample
asv <- data.frame(
  asv = c("a1", "a2", "a3"),
  taxonomy = c("k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Gadiformes;f__Gadidae;g__Gadus;s__morhua",
               "k__Animalia;p__Chordata;c__Actinopteri;o__Gadiformes;f__Gadidae;g__Gadus;s__morhua",
               "k__Animalia;p__Arthropoda;c__Malacostraca;o__Euphausiacea;f__;g__;s__"),
  S1 = c(120, 30, 0), S2 = c(0, 0, 400))
meta <- data.frame(sample = c("S1", "S2"), predator = "grey seal",
                   season = c("winter", "summer"))
long <- dv_from_wide(asv, id_cols = c("asv", "taxonomy"), meta = meta,
                     collapse_by = "taxonomy")
long <- dv_parse_lineage(long, "taxonomy")
spec <- dv_spec(predator = "predator", stomach = "sample",
                prey_name = "prey_name", weight = "reads",
                weight_type = "rra", covariates = "season")
prep <- dv_prepare(long, spec, taxonomy = "columns", verbose = FALSE)
dv_rank_table(dv_tree(prep), "Phylum")
#>        label value_item value_occ pct_occ value_w pct_w
#> 2 Arthropoda          1         1      50       1    50
#> 3   Chordata          1         1      50       1    50
